input: Find a local language exchange partner for Mandarin

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the user's current Mandarin level determines what kind of partner is suitable — a complete beginner needs a very patient native speaker, while an intermediate learner can engage in more fluid conversation.
A language exchange is two-way, so knowing what language the user offers in return is essential — it directly determines who they can partner with and where to search.
Knowing the user's city or region is necessary to find genuinely local options, since platforms, meetup groups, and universities vary by location.
Whether the user wants to meet in person, online, or both changes which platforms and communities to target entirely.
The user's weekly availability and session frequency shapes which partners are a realistic match and how urgently they need to find someone.
Some people want casual conversation practice; others want structured lessons or topic-focused sessions — this shapes what to look for in a partner and how to frame the search.
Understanding the user's end goal — travel, business, HSK exam, cultural interest — defines what 'a good partner' actually means and what to prioritise.

gold.taskTitle: Find a local Mandarin language exchange partner
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to connect with someone nearby to practice Mandarin through a language exchange arrangement.

questions.title: What is your current level of Mandarin?
questions.description: Establish the user's proficiency level (complete beginner, conversational, intermediate, advanced) to identify a compatible partner.

questions.title: What language are you offering in exchange?
questions.description: Identify the language the user speaks natively or fluently, since the exchange is mutual and this defines the partner pool.

questions.title: Which city or area are you based in?
questions.description: Pinpoint the user's location to find relevant local communities, meetup groups, or university language boards.

questions.title: Do you prefer to meet in person or online?
questions.description: Determine the meeting format to narrow down the right platforms and search channels.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you commit to sessions?
questions.description: Understand the user's availability so the plan targets partners with a matching schedule and realistic commitment level.

questions.title: Do you want casual chat or structured topic-based practice?
questions.description: Clarify the preferred style of exchange — free-flowing conversation versus focused, structured sessions — to match the right type of partner.

questions.title: What is your main reason for learning Mandarin?
questions.description: Identify the underlying goal (travel, business, HSK exam, cultural interest, etc.) to define what a successful partnership looks like.
